reports.title: Bath & Body Works Reports Third Quarter Results Exceeding Guidance and Raises Full-Year Sales Outlook

guidance.heading: 2026 Guidance
section: Based on third quarter performance and the company’s current outlook for the fourth quarter, the company is increasing its full-year 2026 net sales guidance to a decline between 3.4% and 2.1% compared to $7,291 million in fiscal 2025. The company is also updating full-year reported earnings per diluted share guidance to between $3.09 and $3.29, compared to $3.11 in fiscal 2025, and maintaining adjusted earnings per diluted share guidance of between $2.60 and $2.80, compared to $3.21 in fiscal 2025.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the company is forecasting net sales to decline between 5.5% and 2.0% compared to $2,724 million in the fourth quarter of 2025. Fourth quarter 2026 earnings per diluted share is expected to be between $1.41 and $1.61, compared to earnings per diluted share of $1.99 and adjusted earnings per diluted share of $2.05 in the fourth quarter of 2025.

desk.headline: Sales down 1% to $1.6bn but beat estimates; adjusted EPS $0.26 well ahead; full-year sales outlook raised, Q4 still seen lower
results: Net sales slipped 1.0% to $1.58bn, but beat the company's own guidance and analyst estimates.
Adjusted EPS fell to $0.26 from $0.35; GAAP EPS halved to $0.19 after $13m of transformation costs and a debt buyback loss.
Store sales fell 4.3%, while online sales grew 2.6% and international/wholesale (Ulta, Amazon) jumped 39%.
Long-term debt is down to $3.4bn from $3.9bn a year ago; a new $500m share buyback was approved.

guidance.summary: Full-year sales are now seen 2.1% to 3.4% lower (raised), with adjusted EPS kept at $2.60–$2.80, in line with estimates. Q4 sales are still expected to fall 2% to 5.5%.

points: Store traffic is still under pressure and inflation weighs on shoppers; management is taking a prudent view of the holidays.
Expects a very promotional Q4; Q4 gross margin guided to about 42.4%, hit by Canadian tariffs and higher oil costs.
New product lines are gaining traction, but seasonal execution was uneven, with Halloween falling short.
Ulta presence grows to about 1,500 stores for the holidays from about 600; Amazon sales described as incremental.
Bought back $250m of 2029 notes; Q3 returned $60m in buybacks and $40m in dividends.
call.source: Call coverage: Investing.com call transcript and Yahoo Finance, 19 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Holiday-quarter sales against the guided 2%–5.5% decline, and how deep promotions go.
Whether online and wholesale growth can offset falling store sales.
Tariff and oil-cost pressure on Q4 margins.
